export const meta = {
  name: 'v1-readiness-grounding',
  description: 'Ground the OST-Agent V1 readiness criteria doc in verified file:line facts across five subsystems',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Investigate', detail: 'five parallel grounded audits of the subsystems the doc must be accurate about' },
    { title: 'Critique', detail: 'completeness critic: what the five missed' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/Users/tanner/dev/OST-Agent'

const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['area', 'facts', 'gaps', 'checkableCriteria'],
  properties: {
    area: { type: 'string' },
    facts: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'Verified mechanical facts, each anchored to file:line. Only what you actually read.',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['claim', 'evidence', 'status'],
        properties: {
          claim: { type: 'string', description: 'One sentence, mechanical and specific' },
          evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'file:line references that prove it' },
          status: { type: 'string', enum: ['built-and-wired', 'built-but-unwired', 'designed-only', 'absent'] },
        },
      },
    },
    gaps: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'What would have to exist for the target architecture, that does not today',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['gap', 'whyItMatters', 'nearestExistingPrecedent'],
        properties: {
          gap: { type: 'string' },
          whyItMatters: { type: 'string' },
          nearestExistingPrecedent: { type: 'string', description: 'The existing file/mechanism a fix should follow, with file:line' },
        },
      },
    },
    checkableCriteria: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'Proposed pass/fail criteria. Each MUST name a concrete mechanical check someone could run.',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['criterion', 'check', 'statusToday'],
        properties: {
          criterion: { type: 'string' },
          check: { type: 'string', description: 'The exact command, test, or observation that decides pass/fail' },
          statusToday: { type: 'string', enum: ['met', 'partially-met', 'not-met', 'unmeasurable-today'] },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}

const CONTEXT = `
You are auditing the repository at ${REPO} (a Claude Code plugin: an append-only MCP server that
maintains a Teresa Torres Opportunity Solution Tree as Obsidian Markdown; the connected Claude Code
session supplies all reasoning; the server is deterministic and holds no model).

The owner wants to reach a V1.0.0 that can run an OST-Agent vault FOR OST-Agent, unattended, and be
trusted to make progress on an arbitrarily large, arbitrarily vague goal. Three architectural
decisions have just been settled by the owner, and your audit must be read against them:

(1) BUILDER ISOLATION. Whoever/whatever builds is given READ-ONLY access to the vault and is
    off-limits from writing it. The builder's only channel back into the tree is the agent's INBOX,
    where it reports NEW DATA PIPELINES / SENSING CHANNELS it has successfully commissioned, in a
    form the agent can digest. The owner has already tried running the builder in the main Claude
    terminal and it failed precisely because that actor could both build AND mutate the tree.

(2) EARNED BELIEVABILITY. A new data stream / result / source arrives untested, untrusted and
    fragile — "like a new employee whose resume, references and self-description are all unverified".
    The agent must reason about a new stream and SELF-DETERMINE its believability by TESTING CAUSE
    AND EFFECT — i.e. a source earns its rung by making predictions that reality corroborates, not by
    declaration.

(3) UNBOUNDED AUTONOMY ENVELOPE, granted in real time by the human's continued presence. The agent
    assumes it has forever, and must be maximally efficient. Feasibility of RESOURCE ACQUISITION is
    itself something to test against the working environment. Example directive: "make a million
    dollars for <named real person> and deposit it to <bank account>" — the agent might propose
    founding a SaaS company, which requires a human to sign legal documents, pitch, raise funding.
    THE HUMAN SPONSOR IS A BUILDER RESOURCE the agent must manage a relationship with. Anything a
    human PROMISES about the runtime environment is exactly as suspect as any other claim and must
    enter through the inbox as evidence. The agent may handle real money and real legal entities
    before the terminal goal is met, using only data from sensing channels it has itself commissioned.

RULES FOR YOUR REPORT:
- Cite file:line for every mechanical claim. Read the code; do not infer from docs alone.
- Sharply distinguish: built-and-wired / built-but-unwired (exists, no caller) / designed-only
  (a doc describes it, no code) / absent.
- This repo's docs sometimes describe REMOVED machinery. Verify existence before repeating a doc.
- Do not propose features. Propose CHECKS — things that pass or fail.
- Be adversarial about safety claims: find where a stated guarantee is discipline rather than mechanism.
`

phase('Investigate')

const AREAS = [
  {
    key: 'builder-isolation',
    prompt: `AREA: Builder isolation and the vault write boundary.

Determine mechanically WHO CAN WRITE THE VAULT today, and what (if anything) would stop a
read-only-intended builder from writing it.

Investigate at least:
- src/ost/vault.ts (the only class touching node files), src/mcp/server.ts, src/security/policy.ts,
  src/security/tools.ts, src/security/validateToolInput.ts, src/git/safe-git.ts, src/mcp/commit.ts
- .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, examples/automation/*, examples/vault/.claude/settings.json
- How OST_VAULT / CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR / CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT determine which directory is the vault
- src/adapters/inbox.ts and src/config/schema.ts: the inbox path, and whether the inbox lives INSIDE
  the vault directory (this matters enormously: if the inbox is inside the vault, a builder that must
  write the inbox cannot be denied filesystem write access to the vault)
- Whether anything mechanically distinguishes "the MCP server writing the vault" from "any process
  with filesystem access writing the vault"
- What git-level protections exist or could exist (the vault is a git repo; commits are made by the server)

Answer concretely: what is the enforcement point for "the builder may read but not write the tree",
and does it exist? What would a commissioning report from a builder have to look like to be digestible
by the ingestion path that exists today (exact format, ids, provenance prefix, idempotency rules)?`,
  },
  {
    key: 'earned-believability',
    prompt: `AREA: Believability, source trust, and whether a rung can be EARNED by tested cause-and-effect.

Map exactly how a claim's weight is currently established, and what is missing for a source to earn
trust through prediction-and-corroboration.

Investigate at least:
- src/knowledge/believability.ts (the ladder, FLOOR_RUNG, ordering), src/knowledge/web-trust.ts
  (HOST_RUNGS, the 'expert' ceiling), src/ost/vault.ts's setEvidence path
- The ost_rank_source and ost_set_evidence tools in src/security/tools.ts — exact arguments, what
  they permit, what they refuse, whether promotion requires any evidence at all
- src/eval/invariants.ts (the evidence-class rule), src/eval/evidence-debt.ts (hasRecordedResult,
  gateSolution), src/ost/results.ts (recordResult — the human-only path)
- src/eval/coverage.ts (thresholds, uncovered statements, bounded/unbounded)
- src/knowledge/unknowns.ts + src/genome/schema.ts (the Unknown contract: Format = stopping condition)

Then answer: is there ANY mechanism today by which a source's track record is measured — i.e. a
prediction recorded, an outcome observed, and the source's rung adjusted as a consequence? If not,
say so plainly and identify the nearest existing precedent to build it on. Pay special attention to
whether an agent can currently promote a source or a node's rung WITHOUT any corroborating measurement,
and to whether ost_rank_source's stated rule ('promote only after a first-party test corroborated the
claim') is enforced by code or merely stated in prose.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'ingestion-contract',
    prompt: `AREA: The inbox / evidence ingestion contract — the single channel a builder and a human sponsor
must both come through.

Establish exactly what an item entering the tree's world looks like, end to end.

Investigate at least:
- src/adapters/inbox.ts, src/adapters/source.ts, src/adapters/friction.ts, src/adapters/transcript.ts,
  src/adapters/usage.ts, src/adapters/tokens.ts, src/adapters/atlassian.ts, src/adapters/slack.ts
- src/processes/tree.ts (readEvidence, getMapped), src/mcp/next-work.ts (how unmapped evidence is
  computed and when something counts as mapped)
- src/mcp/server.ts's ost_ingest_inbox handler and src/security/tools.ts's schema for it
- The evidence record shape on disk: where it lives, its id scheme, provenance prefixes (INBOX:, WEB:,
  SESSION:, USAGE:, FRICTION: — verify which actually exist), idempotency/cursor behaviour

Then answer precisely:
- Which adapters have a live ingestion CALLER and which are built-but-unwired? Verify by grep, do not
  trust the README.
- If an unattended loop runs to `done` with an empty inbox, what — mechanically — could produce the
  next piece of evidence without a human? Name every path that exists today.
- What would a "commissioned sensing channel" have to emit for the tree to ingest it continuously,
  given only what exists? Is there any registry of active sensing channels, or any way for the tree to
  know a channel it commissioned has gone silent?
- Is untrusted ingested content ever able to reach a position where it is read as instruction rather
  than data? Check the tool descriptions and the skill text for injection surface.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'permission-irreversibility',
    prompt: `AREA: Permission, lanes, human-sponsor dependency, and irreversible real-world action.

The target architecture has the agent depending on a human sponsor for signatures, funding, credentials
and spend — and possibly handling real money before the goal is met. Audit what exists to govern that.

Investigate at least:
- src/knowledge/lanes.ts (LANES, computeMayRun, CAUTIOUS_LANE) and src/ost/lanes.ts (setLane,
  flagHumansRequired, suggestCaution, triageLanes, laneConflicts, cautionBacklog)
- The four lanes, and especially `pending-permission` — what it means, how a test leaves that state,
  and whether anything tracks an outstanding request to a human
- src/security/tools.ts: the full tool surface. Enumerate every tool and classify each as read-only /
  append-to-vault / outward-acting. Confirm whether ANY tool can act outside the vault.
- src/web/guard.ts, src/web/reader.ts, src/web/search.ts, src/web/budget.ts, src/web/sources.ts,
  src/web/federated.ts: outward reach, SSRF guard, whether any request is non-GET / can mutate an
  external system, budget refill semantics
- src/git/safe-git.ts (gitPush) and src/config/schema.ts's remote block: what leaves the machine
- src/eval/evidence-debt.ts gateSolution + src/cli/index.ts's `gate` command: the build gate

Then answer:
- Is there any mechanism today that distinguishes a REVERSIBLE action from an IRREVERSIBLE one
  (spending money, signing something, publishing, emailing, creating a legal entity)? If not, say so.
- Is there any accounting of the SCARCE resource in this architecture — human attention and human
  consent — as opposed to compute? What tracks an outstanding ask of the human, its age, or whether
  the human ever answered?
- Where does the trust-model claim "the worst thing it can do is make a commit that doesn't make
  sense" stop being true once a builder and commissioned sensors exist?`,
  },
  {
    key: 'wedge-and-health',
    prompt: `AREA: Wedge conditions, invariant clearability, deterministic health, and scale.

This is a verification task with one specific claim to confirm or refute, plus a systematic audit.

CLAIM TO VERIFY OR REFUTE (be rigorous, read the code, construct the exact sequence):
"A single hard-wrapped [[wikilink]] inside appended prose permanently fails `ost-agent check`
(rule wrapped-wikilink) and CANNOT be cleared through the append-only tool surface, because
wrappedLinkTargets scans the whole body, nothing refuses one at write time, and there is no edit,
delete or rewrite tool. Therefore an unattended loop whose gate is `check` would wedge forever."
Verify against src/ost/node.ts (wrappedLinkTargets), src/eval/invariants.ts, src/ost/vault.ts,
src/security/tools.ts. State explicitly whether it is TRUE, and whether any escape exists.

THEN, systematically: for EVERY rule emitted by checkInvariants (src/eval/invariants.ts) —
single-outcome, dangling-link, wrapped-wikilink, opportunity-connected, solution-mapped,
assumption-mapped, evidence-class, no-self-validation, lane-conflict — determine two things:
  (a) can the agent's own tool surface CREATE this violation?
  (b) can the agent's own tool surface CLEAR it once created?
A rule that can be created but not cleared is a permanent-red wedge. Report the full table.

ALSO:
- Do the same for the hygiene issues in src/mcp/next-work.ts detectHygiene: which are suppressible by
  ost_annotate (verify the suppression mechanism actually works — it filters on node.body containing
  the issue string) and which are not? `done` requires hygieneIssues.length === 0.
- Confirm whether any `loop` command, health record, or .ost-agent/health/runs.jsonl writer exists.
  Check src/cli/index.ts, src/loop/, and grep for callers of detectLaunderedExit.
- Assess computational scale: identify every O(n^2)-or-worse pass over the tree (src/mcp/next-work.ts
  detectHygiene, src/ost/dedupe.ts, src/eval/*), and note that nothing is ever deleted. What breaks
  first as the tree grows to thousands of nodes?`,
  },
]

const findings = await parallel(
  AREAS.map((a) => () =>
    agent(`${CONTEXT}\n\n${a.prompt}`, { label: `audit:${a.key}`, phase: 'Investigate', schema: SCHEMA }),
  ),
)

const good = findings.filter(Boolean)
log(`${good.length}/${AREAS.length} audits returned`)

phase('Critique')

const critic = await agent(
  `${CONTEXT}

Five audits of ${REPO} have just completed. Here is everything they found, as JSON:

${JSON.stringify(good, null, 2)}

Your job is the COMPLETENESS CRITIC pass. You have the same repo available — read it.

Ask, and answer with file:line evidence:
1. What subsystem, failure mode, or wedge condition did all five MISS? Look especially at areas none of
   them were assigned: src/genome/*, src/harness/*, src/eval/attention.ts, src/eval/correlate.ts,
   src/telemetry/*, src/runner/*, src/ost/census.ts, src/ost/dedupe.ts, src/ost/sanitize.ts,
   src/knowledge/ruleset.ts, scripts/gen-skill.ts, and the skill/command generation drift tests.
2. Which of their claims is WRONG or overstated? Verify at least the three most load-bearing claims
   yourself and say plainly if one does not hold.
3. Given the three settled architectural decisions (builder isolation, earned believability, unbounded
   envelope with a human sponsor as a managed resource), what CRITERION is missing that no audit
   proposed — particularly around: the agent's model of its own sponsor relationship; what happens when
   a commissioned sensing channel goes silent or starts lying; how the tree distinguishes its own
   speculation from a sensor's report after both are in the vault as Markdown; and what stops the
   accumulating vault from becoming unreadable at scale given nothing is ever deleted.
4. Name the single ordering constraint that the criteria must respect — the thing that, if built out of
   order, makes everything after it unmeasurable.`,
  { label: 'completeness-critic', phase: 'Critique', schema: SCHEMA, effort: 'high' },
)

return { audits: good, critique: critic }

<tool_use_error>String to replace not found in file.
String:   // Classification and resolution are genome-driven: `class-priority` ranking
  // orders by `klass`, and a klass derived from a compiled-in classifier while
  // the genome declares a different vocabulary would rank against classes that
  // do not exist.
  const allOpenUnknowns: OpenUnknown[] = rankOpenUnknowns(
    tree
      .filter((n) => n.layer === "Unknown" && resolutionState(n) === "open")
      .map((u) => ({
        title: u.title,
        klass: classifyUnknown(u),
        darkens: tree.find((p) => p.layer !== "Unknown" && p.links.includes(u.title))?.title ?? null,
        gaps: contractGaps(u),
      })),
    genome.pivot,
    // Lazily, and only where it is read: the default genome must not pay for a
    // ledger walk on every `ost_next_work`.
    genome.pivot.ranking === "cost-to-resolve" ? costIndex(tree, dir, genome) : undefined,
  );

  // The cap is a display limit, never an amnesty: `done` is computed over every
  // open unknown, and the hidden count is named in the summary. A cap that
  // silently shortened the list would read as "that is all the darkness there is".
  const cap = genome.pivot.maxOpenUnknownsSurfaced;
  const openUnknowns = cap > 0 ? allOpenUnknowns.slice(0, cap) : allOpenUnknowns;
  const hidden = allOpenUnknowns.length - openUnknowns.length;
  const blocksDone = genome.pivot.unknownsBlockDone;

  const done =
    unmappedEvidence.length === 0 &&
    underservedOpportunities.length === 0 &&
    solutionsMissingAssumptions.length === 0 &&
    hygieneIssues.length === 0 &&
    (!blocksDone || allOpenUnknowns.length === 0);</tool_use_error>
